questions.q: What is the difference between defining and generating a recurring journal?
options: They are the same action with different names
Defining sets up the standing accounts/amount logic once; generating creates an actual journal batch for a specific period
Generating happens first, then defining
Defining only applies to Formula journals
questions.explain: A definition is dormant until Generate Recurring Journals creates a real batch for a given period.

questions.q: When you generate a Skeleton recurring journal, what is typically left for the user to do?
options: Enter this period's amount, since accounts are already in place but the amount field is blank
Nothing — it is fully populated
Define the accounts from scratch
Approve the batch automatically
questions.explain: Skeleton journals generate with accounts set but require the amount to be entered manually each period.

questions.q: Does a generated recurring journal batch still need to pass validation before posting?
options: No, generated batches skip validation entirely
Only Formula-type batches need validation
Only if suspense posting is disabled
Yes, it still has to validate (balanced, valid accounts, open period) like any other journal
questions.explain: Automation at the definition stage does not remove the validation, approval, or posting controls covered earlier.

questions.q: What is one way to handle a period where a recurring entry genuinely shouldn't run?
options: Generate it anyway and manually delete the batch afterward
Change its journal category to Adjustment
Simply don't generate it for that period, or give the definition an end date
Disable the entire ledger for that period
questions.explain: Skipping generation for that period, or ending the definition, avoids creating a batch that would need cleanup.

questions.q: What journal source is typically assigned to a batch created by Generate Recurring Journals?
options: Recurring
Manual
Spreadsheet
Allocation
questions.explain: Batches created from recurring journal definitions are sourced as Recurring, distinguishing them from manual or imported entries.
